stem:
Tara learns that parents pass instructions to offspring when living beings reproduce.

Which claim correctly describes what reproduction does?

options.text: Reproduction keeps each type of organism from disappearing and can create small differences that may help survival when conditions change.
Reproduction is the same as growth, so instructions never pass from parents to offspring.
Offspring always match parents exactly, so variation never appears.
Variation erases continuity, so reproduction cannot keep a type of organism going.

teacher.key_rationale: Reproduction creates continuity by passing instructions and can create variation that may help under changing conditions. Treating reproduction as mere growth, denying any variation, or saying variation blocks continuity all miss that hinge.
